title: An injective module has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for every open covering
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the underlying space of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subset and $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of open subsets of $U$ with $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ (any index set), and let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ be the corresponding covering of the Zariski site $X_{\rm Zar}$; here $X_{\rm Zar}$ is the site of open subschemes of $X$ with inclusions as morphisms and jointly surjective open families as coverings [def-sc-zariski-site]; in it the fibre product $U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}$ of opens $U_{i_k}\subseteq U$ is the intersection $U_{i_0\ldots i_p}=U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ with its inclusions (the category is a preordered set, so this is the only choice), and the projection omitting the $j$-th factor is the inclusion $U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}\subseteq U_{i_0\ldots\hat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}$. Let $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ be the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups $W\mapsto\mathcal I(W)$ of $\mathcal I$ on $X_{\rm Zar}$ for $\mathcal U$, i.e. the cohomology of the complex with $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}\mathcal I(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})$ and $d(s)_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j s_{i_0\ldots\hat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}}$. Then $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$. (Stacks states this for any ringed space, together with $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=\mathcal I(U)$, which is not needed here. $\mathcal I$ need not be an injective abelian sheaf, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic] does not apply directly.)

proof.text: For every open $V\subseteq X$, define the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $J_V$ by $J_V(W)=\mathcal O_X(W)$ if $W\subseteq V$ and $J_V(W)=0$ otherwise; restrictions within $V$ are those of $\mathcal O_X$, and any restriction out of a zero group is zero. Since the Zariski site is the poset of opens [def-sc-zariski-site], $J_V(W)=\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)}\mathcal O_X(W)$: there is exactly one summand when $W\subseteq V$ and none otherwise. For $p\geq0$ put $K_p=\bigoplus_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}J_{U_{i_0\ldots i_p}}$ and $K_p=0$ for $p<0$. The inclusion $U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}\subseteq U_{i_0\ldots\widehat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}$ gives $J_{U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}}\to J_{U_{i_0\ldots\widehat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}}$, identity at an open contained in the source and zero otherwise. Let $d_{p+1}:K_{p+1}\to K_p$ be the alternating sum of these maps. On a basis element at any open $W$ this is the alternating deletion differential, so $d_pd_{p+1}=0$ by cancellation of the two orders of deleting each pair of indices.

proof.text: The sheaf $\mathcal I$ is injective also in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$. Indeed, let $a:\mathcal P\hookrightarrow\mathcal Q$ be a monomorphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $f:\mathcal P\to\mathcal I$ a presheaf morphism. The sectionwise exactness of $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and exactness of sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] make $a^\#:\mathcal P^\#\hookrightarrow\mathcal Q^\#$ a monomorphism of sheaves. The adjunction [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives $f^\#:\mathcal P^\#\to\mathcal I$ with $f^\#\eta_{\mathcal P}=f$. Injectivity of $\mathcal I$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends $f^\#$ across $a^\#$ to $g^\#:\mathcal Q^\#\to\mathcal I$. Then $g=g^\#\eta_{\mathcal Q}:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal I$ satisfies $ga=g^\#a^\#\eta_{\mathcal P}=f^\#\eta_{\mathcal P}=f$ by naturality of the sheafification unit. This is the extension property for an injective presheaf.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01EP (lemma-injective-trivial-cech), proof, first sentence; Homology Lemma Tag 015Z (lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives), here expanded using the adjunction

proof.text: For any presheaf $\mathcal P$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] applied to $X_{\rm Zar}$ and $V$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(J_V,\mathcal P)$ with $\mathcal P(V)$ by evaluating a morphism on $1\in J_V(V)$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(K_p,\mathcal P)=\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)}\mathcal P(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})$. If $V'\subseteq V$ and $s\in\mathcal P(V)$, the map corresponding to $s$ sends $1\in J_V(V')$ to $s|_{V'}$; hence precomposition with $J_{V'}\to J_V$ corresponds to the restriction $\mathcal P(V)\to\mathcal P(V')$. Applied to every face of $d_{p+1}$, this identifies the differential $\operatorname{Hom}(K_p,\mathcal P)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K_{p+1},\mathcal P)$ with $s\mapsto(\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j s_{i_0\ldots\widehat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}})$. Therefore $\operatorname{Hom}(K_\bullet,\mathcal P)\cong\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal P)$ as complexes of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex].

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary open $W\subseteq X$ and put $I_W=\{i\in I\mid W\subseteq U_i\}$. By the definition of $J_V$, $K_p(W)$ is the free $\mathcal O_X(W)$-module on $I_W^{p+1}$: $W\subseteq U_{i_0\ldots i_p}$ holds exactly when every $i_j\in I_W$. On these basis elements $d_{p+1}(W)$ deletes one index with sign $(-1)^j$, so $K_\bullet(W)$ is the complex $C_\bullet(I_W;\mathcal O_X(W))$ of [lem-weil-pbc-power-set-complex-contractible]. If $I_W=\varnothing$, every $K_p(W)$ is zero; if $I_W\ne\varnothing$, choose $i_*\in I_W$ and use that node's homotopy $[(i_0,\ldots,i_p)]\mapsto[(i_*,i_0,\ldots,i_p)]$ to obtain $H_p(K_\bullet(W))=0$ for $p>0$. Since kernels and images of presheaves of modules are sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] (1), $\operatorname{im}d_{p+1}=\ker d_p$ as presheaves for every $p>0$. This holds even for an infinite cover, because each basis element and its homotopy have finite support.

proof.text: Let $p>0$ and let $s:K_p\to\mathcal I$ represent a cocycle in $\operatorname{Hom}(K_\bullet,\mathcal I)$, so $s d_{p+1}=0$. By Step 4, $\operatorname{im}d_{p+1}=\ker d_p$; hence $s$ vanishes on $\ker d_p$ and factors uniquely through the epimorphism $K_p\twoheadrightarrow B=\operatorname{im}d_p$, giving $t:B\to\mathcal I$. The inclusion $B\hookrightarrow K_{p-1}$ is a monomorphism, so injectivity of $\mathcal I$ in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$ from Step 2 extends $t$ to $s':K_{p-1}\to\mathcal I$. Then $s=s'd_p$, a coboundary. Thus $H^p(\operatorname{Hom}(K_\bullet,\mathcal I))=0$, and the isomorphism of complexes in Step 3 gives $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. This proves the assertion for every $p>0$.
